The link is specified by linker variables and then the linker is invoked as:
 $(FCL) -o vasp  ..all-objects.. $(LLIBS)

It is mandatory to link VASP to a library for Fast-Fourier transformations (FFT), the lib library, the parser library, and the linear algebra libraries BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK, as well as for the OpenACC GPU port [https://developer.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk NVIDIA HPC-SDK] (≧21.2). Other libraries, e.g., the HDF5 library and Wannier90, are optional.

= Linker variables =

=== FCL ===
:The command that invokes the linker. In most cases:
:<pre>FCL=$(FC) [+ some options]</pre>

:*Using the Intel Composer suite (Fortran compiler + MKL libraries), typically:
:<pre>FCL=$(FC) -mkl=sequential</pre>

=== LLIBS ===
:Specify libraries and/or objects to be linked against, in the usual way:
:<pre>LLIBS=[-L/path/to/installation/lib -llibrary] [/path/to/file/library.a] [/path/to/file/object.o]</pre>

:One has to specify several numerical libraries (BLAS, LAPACK or scaLAPACK, etc).

:For instance, using the Intel Composer suite (and compiling with <code>CPP_OPTIONS= .. -DscaLAPACK ..</code>) this yields:

<blockquote>
<pre>
MKL_PATH   = $(MKLROOT)/lib/intel64
BLACS      = -lmkl_blacs_intelmpi_lp64
SCALAPACK  = $(MKL_PATH)/libmkl_scalapack_lp64.a $(BLACS)
LLIBS      += $(SCALAPACK)
</pre>
</blockquote>

The list of default objects required to compile VASP is given by the variable <code>SOURCE</code> in the <code>/path/to/vasp.X.X.X/src/.objects</code> file.
Objects to be added to this list can be specified in <code>makefile.include</code> by means of:
<pre>OBJECTS= .. your list of objects ..</pre>
In practice, several objects ''must'' be added in this manner, e.g., [[#Fast-Fourier transformation (mandatory)|FFT libraries]].

= Libraries for linear algebra (mandatory) =

To build VASP, you need to link against BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK. Some compiler suites, e.g., the Intel Composer suite, pre-package these libraries, so there is no need to download and build them yourself.

* Using the Intel Composer suite, linking against the BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK libraries that are part of MKL is done as follows:
<blockquote>
<pre>
FCL        = mpiifort -mkl=sequential

MKL_PATH   = $(MKLROOT)/lib/intel64
BLAS       =
LAPACK     =
BLACS      = -lmkl_blacs_intelmpi_lp64
SCALAPACK  = $(MKL_PATH)/libmkl_scalapack_lp64.a $(BLACS)

LLIBS     += $(SCALAPACK) $(LAPACK) $(BLAS)
</pre>
</blockquote>

: In case you use Intel's compilers with OpenMPI instead of Intel-MPI replace the <code>BLACS</code> line above by:
:<pre>BLACS       = -lmkl_blacs_openmpi_lp64</pre>

* For [https://developer.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk NVIDIA HPC-SDK] (>=21.2) that is:
<blockquote>
<pre>
BLAS       = -lblas
LAPACK     = -llapack
SCALAPACK  = -Mscalapack

LLIBS     += $(SCALAPACK) $(LAPACK) $(BLAS)
</pre>
</blockquote>

* When you have built BLAS, LAPACK, and scaLAPACK yourself, you should link against the corresponding shared-objects (<code>lib*.so</code>) as follows:
<blockquote>
<pre>
LIBDIR     = /path/to/my/libs/
BLAS       = -L$(LIBDIR) -lrefblas
LAPACK     = -L$(LIBDIR) -ltmglib -llapack
SCALAPACK  = -L$(LIBDIR) -lscalapack

LLIBS     += $(SCALAPACK) $(LAPACK) $(BLAS)
</pre>
</blockquote>

: To link against a static library object (<code>*.a</code>), for instance for scaLAPACK, replace the <code>SCALAPACK</code> line above by:
:<pre>SCALAPACK  = $(LIBDIR)/libscalapack.a</pre>

= fftw library (mandatory) =

This library provides routines to perform Fast Fourier transformations (FFTs).

=== OBJECTS ===
:Add the objects to be compiled (or linked against) that provide the FFTs (may include static libraries of objects <code>*.a</code>).
:Most probably you are building with <code>-DMPI</code> and want use the FFTs from some <tt>fftw</tt> library (recommended). In that case:
:<pre>OBJECTS = fftmpiw.o fftmpi_map.o fftw3d.o fft3dlib.o</pre> 

=== INCS ===
:For the <tt>fftw</tt> library, i.e.,
:<pre>OBJECTS= .. fftw3d.o fftmpiw.o ..</pre>
:the variable <code>INCS</code> must be set to include the directory that holds <code>fftw3.f</code>:
:<pre>INCS+=-I/path/to/fftw/installation</pre>
:This is needed because <code>fftw3d.F</code> and <code>fftmpiw.F</code> include <code>fftw3.f</code>.
{{NB|mind| If <code>INCS</code> for <tt>fftw</tt> library is not set, then <code>fftw3.f</code> has to be present in <code>/path/to/vasp.X.X.X/src</code>.|:}}

Common choices are:

* When building with the Intel Composer suite it is best to link against the MKL <tt>fftw</tt> wrappers of Intel's FFTs:
<blockquote>
<pre>
FCL = $(FC) -mkl=sequential

OBJECTS = fftmpiw.o fftmpi_map.o fftw3d.o fft3dlib.o
INCS   += -I$(MKLROOT)/include/fftw
</pre>
</blockquote>

* To explicitly link against an <tt>fftw</tt> library (in this case <tt>fftw-3.3.4</tt>):
<blockquote>
<pre>
OBJECTS = fftmpiw.o fftmpi_map.o fftw3d.o fft3dlib.o
FFTW       ?= /path/to/your/fftw-3.3.4
LLIBS      += -L$(FFTW)/lib -lfftw3
INCS       += -I$(FFTW)/include
</pre>
</blockquote>

* For other configurations, please take lead from the <code>makefile.include.your_choice</code> files in <tt>/path/to/vasp.x.x.x/arch</tt> or look at the {{FILE|makefile.include}}.

== Special rules for the optimization level of FFT related objects ==

Based on past experience the optimization level for the compilation of the FFT-related objects is set explicitly.
This is done as follows:

 OBJECTS_O1 += fft3dfurth.o fftw3d.o fftmpi.o fftmpiw.o
 OBJECTS_O2 += fft3dlib.o

= lib library (mandatory) =

The source of this library is included in the VASP distribution. The following variables are related to its configuration:

=== CPP_LIB ===
:The command to invoke the precompiler. In most cases, it is set to:
:<pre>CPP_LIB=$(CPP)</pre>

=== FC_LIB ===
:The command to invoke your Fortran compiler. Usually, set to:
:<pre>FC_LIB=$(FC)</pre>
{{NB|mind| The library can be compiled without MPI support, i.e., when <code>FC{{=}}mpif90</code>, FC_LIB may specify a Fortran compiler without MPI support, e.g.,<code>FC_LIB{{=}}ifort</code>.|:}}

=== FFLAGS_LIB ===
:Fortran compiler flags, including a specification of the level of optimization. In most cases:
:<pre>FFLAGS_LIB=-O1</pre>

=== FREE_LIB ===
:Specifies the options that the Fortran compiler requires to accept free-form source layout, without line-length limitation. In most cases, it will suffise to set:
:<pre>FREE_LIB=$(FREE)</pre>

=== CC_LIB ===
:The command to invoke your C compiler, e.g., gcc, icc, etc.
{{NB|mind|The <tt>lib</tt> library can be compiled without MPI support.|:}}

=== CFLAGS_LIB ===
:C compiler flags, including a specification of the level of optimization. In most cases:
:<pre>CFLAGS_LIB=-O</pre>

=== OBJECTS_LIB ===
:List of "non-standard" objects to be added to the library. In most cases:
:<pre>OBJECTS_LIB= linpack_double.o</pre>

:When compiling VASP with [[Precompiler options#-Duse_shmem|-Duse_shmem]], one has to add <code>getshmem.o</code> as well, i.e., add the following line:
:<pre>OBJECTS_LIB+= getshmem.o</pre>

= parser library (mandatory) =

The source of this library is included in the VASP distribution. The following variables are related to its configuration:

=== CXX_PARS ===
:The command to invoke your C++ compiler, e.g., g++, icpc, etc.

The <tt>parser</tt> needs to be linked against a ''C++ Standard'' library.
If this is not already part of the definition of <code>FCL</code> it can be added to the [[Compiler options|compiler option]] <code>LLIBS</code>.
When using the Intel Composer suite this would amount to:

 LLIBS += -lstdc++

= QD library =

The QD library is included in [https://developer.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk NVIDIA HPC SDK] ≧ 21.2 and supports quadruple precision arithmetic.
Add the following lines to your {{FILE|makefile.include}}:

 NVROOT     ?= /path/to/nvidia/hpc_sdk/Linux_x86_64/version
 QD         ?= $(NVROOT)/compilers/extras/qd
 LLIBS      += -L$(QD)/lib -lqdmod -lqd
 INCS       += -I$(QD)/include/qd
{{NB|tip|The following line might help to find the NVIDIA root:}} 
 NVROOT      =$(shell which nvfortran | awk -F /compilers/bin/nvfortran '{ print $$1 }')
{{NB|important|As of [https://developer.nvidia.com/hpc-sdk NVIDIA HPC SDK] {{=}} 21.2, the library path of the QD library needs to be added manually to the system environment:}}
 export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:$(NVROOT)/compilers/extras/qd/lib

= Optional libraries =

See [[Makefile.include#Customize|how to customize the makefile.include file]] to find an overview of optional libraries.
